coherence_suite._requires_coreference: features.coreference needs the 'fastcoref' package (which pulls in torch and a transformer encoder) plus a one-time download of its default model (biu-nlp/f-coref, ~90M parameters); without it, every discourse.coherence_*_coref metric id reports 'unavailable' with that reason. The flag defaults to false and this note is stripped before it ever reaches the metric, so nothing downloads unasked.
coherence_suite._requires_lexical_wordnet: features.lexical_wordnet and features.lexical_wordnet_hypernym both need the nltk 'wordnet' corpus downloaded (python -m nltk.downloader wordnet) -- the nltk package alone is not enough. Without it, discourse.coherence_lexical_chain_coverage_wordnet and discourse.coherence_lexical_chain_coverage_hypernym report 'unavailable' with that instruction; every other channel is unaffected.
coherence_suite._requires_semantic: features.semantic needs 'sentence-transformers' installed to embed with the model named by semantic_model (default all-MiniLM-L6-v2, downloaded on first use). Without it, the semantic findings degrade to a TF-IDF lexical-overlap proxy rather than disappearing, and each finding's warning/distribution.backend says so.
coherence_suite._requires_entity_graph: the entity co-occurrence graph metric ids (discourse.coherence_entity_graph_density and its _coref variant) need 'networkx'; without it they report 'unavailable' while the rest of the entity/coreference groups, which only need spaCy, are unaffected.
coherence_suite._requires_transition_corpus_delta: discourse.coherence_entity_grid_transition_corpus_delta needs a corpus profile built with coherence_suite enabled AND BOTH --parse-metrics and --model-metrics (this suite's cost is 'parse' and it requires sentence_transformers, so textgrader.corpus._metric_names needs both flags before it will call this suite's profile_vector); without one it reports 'no corpus entity-grid transition profile available'.

randomness_suite._complexity_measures_requires: needs numpy for the permutation/spectral/SVD/ApEn/SampEn family; without it every one of those five findings reports 'unavailable' (the Lempel-Ziv complexity finding in the same feature is dependency-free and still runs).
randomness_suite._lexical_gibberish_requires: unknown_word_rate needs wordfreq (pip install wordfreq); without it that one finding reports 'unavailable' -- letter_frequency_divergence, consonant_cluster_rate, immediate_repeat_rate and char_run_length_entropy in this same feature are dependency-free and still run.
randomness_suite._compression_requires: zlib/gzip/bz2/lzma are stdlib and always work. zstd/brotli/lz4/ppmd each need their own pip package (zstandard/brotli/lz4/pyppmd); snappy needs python-snappy AND the system libsnappy-dev package (apt/brew, not pip). Any one missing degrades only its own compression_ratio_<name> finding to 'unavailable'.
randomness_suite._pos_dependency_requires: needs the shared spaCy parse (spacy + a downloaded model, e.g. `python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm`); without it every finding in this feature reports 'unavailable'. Off by default because it forces a parse cost onto every user regardless of whether they wanted this one channel.
randomness_suite._ppm_language_model_requires: needs pyppmd (pip install pyppmd); without it ppm_cross_entropy reports 'unavailable'.
randomness_suite._letter_bigram_divergence_requires: needs the shipped data/prose_reference.json corpus profile (its word_frequency table); without it, or if it is unreadable, letter_bigram_divergence reports 'unavailable' naming the missing/broken file.
randomness_suite._kenlm_language_model_requires: needs the `kenlm` Python wheel (query-time bindings) AND a compiled `lmplz` trainer binary that pip cannot provide -- build KenLM from source (a C++ compiler and Boost; see https://github.com/kpu/kenlm#compiling), then put the resulting `lmplz` on PATH or set kenlm_lmplz_path to its full path. Without either, kenlm_cross_entropy reports 'unavailable' naming exactly which piece (the wheel or the trainer) is missing and how to get it; nothing else in this suite is affected.
randomness_suite._neural_language_model_requires: needs torch + transformers (multi-gigabyte install; the configured neural_lm_model, distilgpt2 by default, is downloaded or read from a local cache on first use). Without either package, neural_lm_perplexity reports 'unavailable'. Caveat even when available: subword (BPE) tokenization can score purely random letters as MORE 'fluent' (lower perplexity) than grammatically word-order-scrambled real prose, so this channel is NOT a gibberish detector -- see the module docstring and this feature's own finding.distribution.warning_not_a_gibberish_detector.
randomness_suite._textdescriptives_cross_check_requires: needs its own spaCy pipeline plus the textdescriptives package (pip install textdescriptives); without either, textdescriptives_word_perplexity reports 'unavailable'.

_requires.nli_entailment: needs `transformers` (pip install transformers torch) plus a downloaded model checkpoint (nli_model, cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-small by default, fetched from Hugging Face on first use). This is the most expensive channel in this suite: loading the pipeline costs about 2.5s and scoring costs roughly 30ms/pair on an otherwise-idle CPU core, before nli_max_pairs even grows large. Without transformers or a reachable checkpoint, discourse.logic_nli_label_distribution and discourse.logic_nli_heuristic_agreement report 'unavailable' with the reason; no other feature in this suite is affected, and no model is ever loaded unless this key is explicitly true.
_requires.coreference_resolution: needs `fastcoref` (pip install fastcoref) plus its packaged model (biu-nlp/f-coref, fetched from Hugging Face on first use), loaded through textgrader.optional.shim_fastcoref_transformers to stay compatible with transformers 5.x. Without fastcoref, or if it fails to load, every pronoun-subject proposition is simply excluded from cross-sentence matching -- exactly the same result as leaving this feature off, just with a reason recorded instead of silence. This is a modifier, not a metric group of its own: it changes what feeds `propositions`, `nli_entailment`, `lexical_opposition` and `temporal_ordering` rather than adding metric ids.
_requires.lexical_opposition: needs `nltk` (pip install nltk) AND its WordNet corpus data downloaded separately -- the package alone is not enough. Run python -c "import nltk; nltk.download('wordnet')" once. Without the corpus data, discourse.logic_wordnet_antonym_candidates and discourse.logic_wordnet_hypernym_downgrade_rate report 'unavailable' with that exact command in the reason.
_requires.temporal_ordering: needs `python-dateutil` (pip install python-dateutil). Without it, discourse.logic_temporal_order_candidates reports 'unavailable'; the 'temporal' subtype inside discourse.logic_entity_attribute_conflict_candidates (features.propositions) is unaffected either way, since it only notices two differing years/dates, never orders them.
_requires.semantic_role_labeling: needs `transformers` (already required by nli_entailment; no new package) plus a downloaded checkpoint (srl_model, cu-kairos/propbank_srl_seq2seq_t5_small by default, fetched from Hugging Face on first use). One model-generation call per clause-level predicate examined (capped by srl_max_predicates, much smaller than proposition_cap because each call is far more expensive than the shared spaCy parse). Without transformers or a reachable checkpoint, discourse.logic_srl_role_pattern_consistency and discourse.logic_srl_argument_omission_rate report 'unavailable' with the reason.
_requires.relation_extraction: needs `transformers` (no new package) plus a downloaded checkpoint (relation_extraction_model, Babelscape/rebel-large by default, ~1.6GB, fetched from Hugging Face on first use). CLOSED-schema relation extraction (~200 Wikidata-style relation types), not open-domain OpenIE -- AllenNLP's OpenIE predictor cannot be installed here (see the module docstring's quoted pip dry-run failure) and Stanford OpenIE is Java. Hand-checked, not assumed: a plain fictional sentence stating nothing about where a character lives still generated a plausible-sounding 'residence' triple the text never asserts, so this channel is not simply quiet on fiction -- it can invent a schema-compatible relation instead of finding none. Without transformers or a reachable checkpoint, both discourse.logic_relation_extraction_* metrics report 'unavailable'.
_requires.argument_mining: needs `transformers` (no new package) plus a downloaded checkpoint (argument_mining_model, raruidol/ArgumentMining-EN-ARI-AIF-RoBERTa_L by default, ~1.4GB, fetched from Hugging Face on first use). A real Argument Relation Identification classifier (No-Relation/Inference/Conflict/Rephrase) applied to this suite's own therefore/because/however-adjacent clause pairs; connective_chain_length (features.connective_relations) stays a separate, unchanged, honestly-named proxy. Without transformers or a reachable checkpoint, both discourse.logic_argument_relation_* metrics report 'unavailable'.

timeseries_suite._requires_catch22_and_catch24: pycatch22 (pip install pycatch22). Without it, every catch22_* feature group and both catch24_raw_mean/catch24_raw_variance report 'unavailable' with an install hint instead of a number.
timeseries_suite._requires_wavelets: PyWavelets (pip install PyWavelets). Without it, wavelet_energy and wavelet_entropy report 'unavailable' with an install hint instead of a number.
timeseries_suite._requires_stationarity: statsmodels (pip install statsmodels) for a real Augmented Dickey-Fuller test. Without it, the 'stationarity' feature group does NOT go unavailable: it falls back to a labelled, weaker half-split standardized mean-gap proxy and says so in its warning.
timeseries_suite._requires_change_points: ruptures (pip install ruptures) for real PELT change-point search. Without it, the 'change_points' feature group does NOT go unavailable: it falls back to a labelled single-split maximum-mean-shift scan (at most one change point can ever be found) and says so in its warning.
timeseries_suite._requires_embedding_sequences: sentence-transformers (pip install sentence-transformers, in requirements-embeddings.txt) plus a downloaded sentence-embedding model (embedding_model above, default all-MiniLM-L6-v2, fetched on first use). Needed only if 'sequences' explicitly names sentence_similarity_prev or sentence_distance_centroid -- neither is ever selected by default. Without it, both sequences fall back to a TF-IDF lexical-overlap proxy, a different quantity, labelled as such (backend=lexical) in every finding's warning.
timeseries_suite._requires_tsfresh: tsfresh (pip install tsfresh). Needed only if 'feature_groups' explicitly names 'tsfresh' -- it is never selected by default. Without it, the 'tsfresh' feature group reports 'unavailable' with an install hint instead of a number.

stylometry_suite._embedding_style_requires: sentence-transformers plus a one-time model download (~90MB for the default all-MiniLM-L6-v2); without it, embedding_style/embedding_reference findings and the impostors_representation='embedding' branch degrade to unavailable() with that reason. Never loads on its own -- see the module docstring's 'The critical gating rule'.
stylometry_suite._embedding_reference_requires: a corpus profile built with THIS SAME suite's features.embedding_style also enabled at profiling time (rebuild it with textgrader.corpus so feature_profiles['stylometry_suite'] holds per-book embedding vectors), plus sentence-transformers available at grading time to embed the manuscript the same way. Enabling embedding_reference alone, without rebuilding the profile, degrades to unavailable().
stylometry_suite._ncd_against_corpus_requires: ncd_corpus_dirs pointed at one or more directories of readable reference .txt/.md files, present on disk at GRADING time (not just when the corpus profile was built -- this measurement reads the folder directly, it is never served from the cached profile). Without a reachable directory this degrades to unavailable() naming what was missing.
stylometry_suite._impostors_requires: a corpus profile with author metadata (metadata.author on at least impostors_min_authors+1 books). impostors_representation='embedding' additionally needs the same profile rebuilt with features.embedding_style enabled (see _embedding_reference_requires).
stylometry_suite._pos_dependency_requires: spaCy (en_core_web_sm) for the shared parse this feature forces -- tens of seconds on a novel-length manuscript; off by default for cost, not because it needs an unusual package.
stylometry_suite._lexicalrichness_crosscheck_requires: the lexicalrichness package; without it this degrades to unavailable() and every other group in the suite is unaffected.
stylometry_suite._corpus_reference_dependent_features: corpus_reference, word_frequency_distance, author_language_model, corpus_language_model and impostors all read the corpus_profile configured at the project level; without one configured (or reachable), each degrades to unavailable() rather than failing the run.
